title: Components of a product with a geometrically irreducible scheme
statement: Let $K$ be a field, let $U$ be a geometrically irreducible scheme over $K$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and let $V$ be any scheme over $K$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Then the projection $U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}V\to V$ induces a bijection between the irreducible components of $U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}V$ and the irreducible components of $V$ [def-weil-irreducible-components].

proof.text: Let $p:U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}V\to V$ be the second projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. (a) $p$ is open: it is the base change of the structure morphism $U\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ along $V\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-base-change], so [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open] applied to the $K$-scheme $U$ and $S=V$ says that $p$ is an open map. (b) For $y\in V$ with residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field], the scheme-theoretic fibre $(U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}V)\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ is, by the universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] (pasting of cartesian squares), isomorphic to the base change $U_{\kappa(y)}=U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ along the field extension $\kappa(y)/K$ [def-pc-field-extension], which is irreducible because $U$ is geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] the first projection of the scheme-theoretic fibre is a homeomorphism onto the set-theoretic fibre $p^{-1}(y)$, so $p^{-1}(y)$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] for every $y\in V$.

proof.text: By step 1 the continuous map $p$ of underlying spaces is open and all of its fibres $p^{-1}(y)$ are irreducible. Hence [lem-sc-open-map-irreducible-fibres-components] applies to $p$: $T\mapsto p^{-1}(T)$ is a bijection from the irreducible components of $V$ to those of $U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}V$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], with inverse $W\mapsto p(W)$. This is the bijection induced by the projection.
